catalogue_requests.summary: Blink the device indicator LED through the native Device.blink sequence.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null, the hardware backend (native.py) was never imported or run, no hardware was attached, and no hardware run is claimed.

Recon: the card's entry symbol my_app.classes.device:Device exists at my_app/classes/device.py:34. Device creates Port objects for positions 1 through 16 (device.py:57-58), discovery enumerates U3 devices (89-108), connect opens u3.U3 by serial number (112-120), rename writes the firmware name (122-132) and blink flashes the indicator (134-148). The real measurement entry point is the module function timecourse.measure_voltage (59-92), not a Device method; measure_temp (97-105) reads the internal temperature. The card's hints (Experiment.write_outfile_header, start_experiment, start_subproc, stop_experiment) are app-level CSV and process management in my_app/classes/experiment.py, not the instrument interface, so they are not exposed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the helper hint PythonObjectDriver is not used. The package is a direct Driver over Device because the measurement reaches the U3 handle returned by Device.connect, the driver needs an @action bound to cap.measure.voltage.v1, an x-cap action with an inline output schema, a read/write pair for the firmware name, and an @estop; the fixed family tables cannot express these. The card's candidate cap.device.configure.v1 is used for the name write.

Shape and G7: the fake's top-level class implements only Device.connect, Device.rename and Device.blink. Its nested _FakeU3 stands in for the u3.U3 handle that Device.connect documents returning; it implements configIO (used at timecourse.py:68), getAIN (the U3 convenience analog read) and close. No upstream clone code was imported or run. The measurement maps ports 1-16 to AIN0-15 as the clone does (timecourse.py:65-68), sets the FIO/EIO analog mask, reads one calibrated analog input and closes the handle in a finally block. The DAC power-on/off sequence (timecourse.py:70-83, 5 V and 2.6 V at 11-16) is in native.py on the hardware path only.

NOT COVERED: the hardware backend and all hardware behaviour; the upstream n_reps=9 average (the driver returns one calibrated sample per call); the internal temperature read; Device.discovery and the experiment lifecycle (start/stop subprocess, pickle/config state, CSV output); calibration from Calibration.tsv; port usage assignment and simultaneous 16-port scans (one channel per call); the USB and power wiring. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording.

Limits: none. The only write is the string firmware name, the measurement input is a string port enum 1-16, and the blink action has no input; the clone states no numeric bound the driver could declare, so no Limit or Limit.operator_required is used and no site-limits overlay is needed. No Limit was invented. The only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: SAFE-014 has no limited actuating capability to probe because there is no numeric actuating input; no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning occurred.

Safety: risk R1 matches the card floor and cap.device.configure.v1's floor. The clone describes LEDs/sensors and analog voltage measurement, no heater, pump, laser, motion axis or high-force actuator. The @estop opens and closes a U3 handle, and the latch refuses writes and invokes; the measurement action is a read class, so reads remain allowed after the latch, as the runtime defines. The e-stop does not interrupt a blocking getAIN and is not a safety-rated stop. No clone text documents an independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set; SAFE-045 applies only at R2/R3. The loader does not refuse this R1 package's hardware backend; running it is an operator decision, and this package claims no such protection.

Kind: device_kind sensor because cap.measure.voltage.v1 binds instrument.dmm, instrument.smu and sensor, and the clone's scalar output is a calibrated analog voltage; cap.measure.intensity.v1 or cap.measure.spectrum.v1 would mislabel that voltage as intensity or spectra.

Catalogue request: x-cap.natlabrockies.blink.v1 for Device.blink; no catalogue class blinks or identifies an indicator LED.

Verification: the gate passed G1-G7 and G9; G8 is warn on SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE. The package cases in test_driver.py add the identity and 16 ports, the firmware-name write, port voltages on channels 1 and 16, invalid channel refusal, blink and the e-stop latch. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every run.
